subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should TUI auto-follow be fixed as a renderer bug only, exposed as a user-visible TUI mode or setting, or handled as both?
rationale: Source inspection supports a credible renderer/update path, but changing terminal follow behavior affects default TUI UX and may require a new persisted setting rather than a narrow code repair.

options.title: Set TUI anchoring policy plus visible control
options.body: Add a TUI-owned near-bottom/off/always or equivalent mode with live PTY proof and keep browser WebChat settings separate.

options.title: Fix only the renderer jump path
options.body: Patch the pi-tui or OpenClaw render path to avoid disruptive full redraws without adding a new user-facing setting.

options.title: Start with the narrower scrollback issue
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78017 as the first fix target and revisit this broader auto-follow request after live proof.

recommendation.title: Set TUI anchoring policy plus visible control
recommendation.body: Add a TUI-owned near-bottom/off/always or equivalent mode with live PTY proof and keep browser WebChat settings separate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history put them closest to the current TUI render/session lifecycle and the product-shape decision.
